cards.front: What decides which overloaded method runs?
cards.back: The static types of the arguments, at compile time
cards.extra: Overload resolution never looks at the object — which is why passing a subtype reference can pick a different overload than the runtime type suggests.
cards.source: digitalocean.com — Overriding vs Overloading in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::13 Method Overloading and Overriding

cards.front: What decides which overridden method runs?
cards.back: The runtime type of the object, not the declared type of the variable
cards.extra: Parent p = new Child(); p.work(); runs Child's version. That is dynamic dispatch.
cards.source: digitalocean.com — Overriding vs Overloading in Java

cards.front: Where do mistakes surface for overloading versus overriding?
cards.back: Overloading: at compile time (no matching signature). Overriding: at run time (the wrong method is silently called)
cards.extra: A misspelled override is not an override at all — it compiles and the parent's method still runs, which is why @Override matters.
cards.source: digitalocean.com — Overriding vs Overloading in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::13 Method Overloading and Overriding

cards.front: Can overloading happen across a class hierarchy?
cards.back: Yes — a subclass method with the same name but different parameters overloads the inherited one
cards.extra: The article says overloading happens "in the same class", which is the common case but not the rule. Overriding, by contrast, requires a superclass/subclass pair.
cards.source: digitalocean.com — Overriding vs Overloading in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::13 Method Overloading and Overriding

cards.front: What must match for a method to be an override?
cards.back: The entire signature — name and parameter types — plus a compatible return type
cards.extra: Different parameter types make it an overload, not an override, even if the names are identical: process(int[]) does not override process(Object[]).
cards.source: digitalocean.com — Overriding vs Overloading in Java
cards.merge_into: 00 Java Roadmap::02 Object Model::13 Method Overloading and Overriding

cards.front: Why is overriding called runtime polymorphism and overloading compile-time polymorphism?
cards.back: Because the method body is chosen by the JVM at run time versus by the compiler from the declared types
cards.extra: Only overriding is polymorphism in the strict sense; overloading is static selection among distinct methods that share a name.
cards.source: digitalocean.com — Overriding vs Overloading in Java
